Likely to be the northern Pakistan town of Sialkot which was once called Sagala or Sangala. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sagala)
Jiankang, originally called Jianye. It's name was changed to Nanjing during the Ming dynasty. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiankang)
1122-1153CE. Also Huiningfu or Shangjing Huiningfu, in what is now Acheng District, Harbin, Heilongjiang Province. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huiningfu)
Zhongdu was located in what is now the southwestern part of Beijing's Xicheng District. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhongdu)
1233-1234 CE. In what is now called Runan County. Also previously called Ancheng County and Ruyang County.
Shengle is located at present-day Xiyaozi and Tuchengzi village. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shengle)
Also Chang'an and now called Xi'an.
Chang'an is the traditional name for what is now called Xi'an.

Administrative capital near Xi'an is Hao. "Fenghao (simplified Chinese: 沣镐; traditional Chinese: 灃鎬; pinyin: Fēnghào) is the modern name of the twin city formed by the Western Zhou capitals of Feng and Hao.." (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fenghao)
Also called Khanbaliq, in what is now modern-day central Beijing.
Also known as Per-Banebdjedet, Anpet, and now as Tell El-Ruba.
Thebes was within what is now the city of Luxor.
Eventually incorporated into Cairo. the only surviving structure is the Mosque of Ibn Tulun which are the coordinates given.
Exact location of Benakataka is unknown but it is thought to be in the Nashik region.
Capital 1336-1565 CE. Within area of Hampi.
Nisa or Parthaunisa, and was later renamed Mithradātkert.
Referred to as Hekatompylos in Chinese sources but is also knows as Qumis or Hecatompylos.
Also Ecbatana. Thought to be Hagmatana Hill (Tappe-ye Hagmatāna) in Hamadan Province of Iran. (Brown 1997: 80–84)
The site of is Ctesiphon approximately in the location of modern day Al-Mada'in.
Dastgerd (romanised as Dastagird) was a capital only during the reign of Khurau II.
Also Ectatana. Thought to be Hagmatana Hill (Tappe-ye Hagmatāna) in Hamadan Province of Iran. (Brown 1997: 80–84)
Shahr-e-Rey also referred to as Ray or Rayy.
645-672 CE. Now Naniwa Ward in Osaka.
Fujiwara-kyō, in what is now Kashihara in Nara Prefecture.
Burana Tower is now located at the site of what was Balasagun.

Seshat wiki has coded the capital as Ch'ien-Ch'üan, but I cannot find this anywhere. (http://seshatdatabank.info/browser/KgWTurk) However Wikipedia, in several entries, states that there were two capitals: Suyab or Ak-beshim (principle capital) and Navekat (summer capital), which I have coded here. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Turkic_Khaganate)
Yasodharapura (later called Angkor) was the capital in 889-922ce and 922-1080ce.
Also Phnom Kulen. Capital in 802 CE.
Modern city of Sambor Prei Kuk.

Also referred to as Nafuna. Exact location unknown, but some historians have suggested this may have been an alternative name for Angkor Borei (or a closeby settlement) which is also referred to as Vyädhapura and as T'e-mu in Chinese sources. (Coedes 1968: 36-37) Though this is debated. (Vickery 1998: 19)
"The East Capital was near city of Liao-yang in the area of settlement of Bohai peoples." (Kradin 2014: 153)

Location unknown. "Early in the 6th century, probably under Anagui's reign, the Rouran built their capital city, the town of Mumocheng, encircled with two walls constructed by Liang shu (LS 54: 47a-47b; Taskin 1984, p. 290)... However, no trace of the town has been found to date and historians argue about its location." (Kradin 2005: 163) However, an earlier capital - Gansu - was located in what is now Gansu province of Northwest China (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rouran_Khaganate) Therefore I have used those coordinates for this potential capital location.

1241-1317 CE. "The ruins of Mohammad Tur are situated on the route of Badin-Sujawal road, near Ghari Wah about three kilometers away, in tapo and deh Shah Kapur, in south in Jati taluka." (http://heritage.eftsindh.com/pending.php?id=1250/thatta/thatta-muhammad-tur) Can't find exact placement on map and no sources confirm this but I have provided a location of Jati.
Capital 800-716 BCE. Located at the site of modern-day Karima, Sudan.

The capital was Balkh (Bactria), which the Chinese referred to as Chien-shih. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balkh) Although the seshat wiki has coded Chien-shih as the capital,I have changed it here to Balkh to keep in line with the known names. (http://seshatdatabank.info/browser/AfTochr)
In Huanbei District on the outskirts of what is now Anyang.
Also called Bo. In the area of modern-day Zhengzhou.
Exact location is not known. These coordinates are to the pyramid of Amenemhet I who built the capital of Itjtawyamenemhat.
Also known as Thinis. Approximate location is at modern-day Girga.
Avaris was located at the modern site of Tell el-Daba.
Madrid: 1561-1601 CE; Valladolid: 1601-1606 CE; Madrid: 1606-1700 CE
Madrid: 1561-1601 CE; Valladolid: 1601-1606 CE; Madrid: 1606-1700 CE
Kumase or Kumasi. Now officially spelled Coomassie.

The capital was in the mid-ninth century moved to another site in Central Java, Mamrati, and then again around half a century later to Poh Pitu. (Poesponegoro and Notosusanto 2008: 159) Exact location is unknown but may have been in the Kedu Plain, somewhere around the modern Magelang or Temanggung regencies. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mataram_Kingdom) Marked location as Megelang.

Unsure of exact location for this capital. When Medang moved to East Java around 929, the capital was placed firstly at Tamwlang for a very short time, and then moved to Watu Galuh. (Brown 2004: 68) "According to Turyan inscription (dated 929), Sindok moved the capital to Tamwlang and later moved it again to Watugaluh. Historians identify those names with the Tambelang and Megaluh area near modern Jombang, East Java." (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mataram_Kingdom) Have marked location as Tambelang.

Exact location is unknown but may have been in the Kedu Plain, somewhere around the modern Magelang or Temanggung regencies. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mataram_Kingdom) Have marked location as Temanggung.
Identified as the Wotun area of modern-day Madiun.
Identified with the site of Tel-Balata.
Capital 950-900 BCE. Generally accepted to be at the site of Tel Fara but could also be where the nearby town of Tayasir is located.
Sosavur was located in now present-day Angadi in Kerala.
Halebidu (or Halebeedu or Halebid) is the modern name for Dvarasamudram.
Regional capital from 460-? CE. May have been the area of present day Devagiri (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kadamba_dynasty)
Shahjahanabad is present day Delhi. Capital from 1648-1857 CE.

The exact location of Agade (or Akkad) is unknown but is thought to have possibly been near the river Tigris somewhere between Baghdad and Samarra. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akkad_(city); Foster 2016: 14) I have markled the town of Tarmiyah which is approx halfway between Samarra and Baghdad and on the banks of the Tigris.

Originally shown as Kar-Maduk. Although the capital city was Babylon, it was the city of Kar-Marduk where the king resided, potentially as this was located in a less vulnerable area. (Liverani 2014: 364-370) Therefore have changed to Babylon.

"Unfortunately, the centre of the Elamite confederation, the Awan region, from which the Elamite royal family took its name, has not yet been located... other Elamite centres, such as Susa (Which was in close contact with Mesopotamia) and Anshan (Tall-i Malyan), have been located." (Leverani 2014: 142) "Awan was a city-state or possibly a region of Elam whose precise location is not certain, but it has been variously conjectured to be north of Susa, in south Luristan, close to Dezful, or Godin Tepe." (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Awan_dynasty) I have marked as Dezful.
Now called Chogha Zanbil and built by the king, Untash-Napirish.
Also called Anzan or Ansan, in modern day Tall-e Malyan.

Also known as Hidali or Hidala. Exact location unknown. "According to Assyrian annals, Hidali was in a mountainous region, and, according to Achaemenid Elamite administrative texts, it was a little more than halfway along the road from Persepolis to Susa. Proposed locations include Behbahān, Kuhgiluya, and the region between Rām-Hormuz and Behbahān." (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/hidali) Have marked as Behbahān.
Have used the coordinates for the Kofun tomb of Emperor Nintoku as Kawachi as a definitive city/site isn't available.
